answer: One concrete defense is a refundable bond behind every agent address, tracked in a public cipher-secured ledger so no one can hide a second identity behind the same funds. Because the bond scales with the work an agent may perform, spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds, and any fault forfeits all of it. That creates a thin thread of accountability linking each identity to real value at risk, so sybils become an expensive bet. Not a velvet glove: enforcement is automatic.
